cell_type_context: mouse bone-marrow-derived and peritoneal macrophages; human monocytes
compartment_context: plasma membrane; cytoplasm; nucleus; gene promoter
context_scope: primary model context only; no SCI transfer inferred
assay_or_perturbation: IL-4 stimulation; receptor-chain deficiency/blockade; STAT6 phosphorylation and DNA-binding assays; Arg1 RT-PCR; receptor-reconstitution and kinase-deficiency comparisons
citation_note: Junttila et al. 2008, J Exp Med; primary mouse BMDM/peritoneal macrophage and human monocyte study
evidence_summary: The primary study links IL-4 receptor composition to STAT6 activation and IL-4-induced Arg1 expression, with type-I receptor and STAT6 dependence in macrophages.
limitations: Arg1 is a measured gene-expression output; the paper does not establish a universal receptor composition across cell types or an SCI receiver-cell response; no new causal edge is asserted

cell_type_context: primary human macrophages derived from blood monocytes
compartment_context: plasma membrane; cytoplasm; nucleus; gene promoter
context_scope: primary model context only; no SCI transfer inferred
assay_or_perturbation: IL-10 stimulation; JAK and STAT3 inhibition; NGAL promoter-reporter deletion and site mutagenesis; STAT3/C/EBPbeta decoy and ChIP assays; LCN2 mRNA and protein-release measurements
citation_note: Peyrin-Biroulet et al. 2012, J Leukoc Biol; primary human macrophage IL-10/STAT3/NGAL study
evidence_summary: The primary study supports an IL-10-JAK/STAT3 route to LCN2/NGAL promoter activation and expression, with STAT3 and C/EBPbeta promoter occupancy.
limitations: C/EBPbeta cooperates with STAT3; LCN2 protein release was measured in the same model but is not treated as an automatic receptor-mediated downstream edge; no SCI transfer inferred

cell_type_context: naive and polarized mouse CD4-positive T cells; Th17 cells
compartment_context: plasma membrane; cytoplasm; nucleus; gene promoter
context_scope: primary model context only; no SCI transfer inferred
assay_or_perturbation: IL-21 stimulation or blockade; STAT3-deficient comparisons; IL17A expression and IL-17 production assays; promoter binding analysis
citation_note: Wei et al. 2007, J Biol Chem; primary Th17 IL-21/STAT3/IL-17 study
evidence_summary: The primary study reports IL-21-induced IL-17 production and expression in a STAT3-dependent manner and identifies direct STAT3 binding to the IL21 promoter.
limitations: The paper is an autocrine Th17 differentiation model and does not establish an SCI receiver-cell endpoint; the IL21R/JAK layer is retained from receptor-proximal primary evidence and is not expanded into additional adaptor edges

cell_type_context: murine B-lineage cells and heterologous TSLPR/IL7RA receptor-reconstitution systems
compartment_context: plasma membrane; cytoplasm; nucleus; gene promoter
context_scope: primary model context only; no SCI transfer inferred
assay_or_perturbation: TSLP stimulation; Stat5 DNA-complex formation; CIS transcription; TSLP-R/IL-7Ralpha receptor reconstitution; Stat5 requirement and kinase-deficient comparisons
citation_note: Isaksen et al. 1999, J Immunol; primary TSLP/STAT5/CIS response study
evidence_summary: The primary study supports TSLP receptor-complex signaling to functional Stat5 and transcription of the Stat5-responsive gene CIS.
limitations: The study supports a STAT5-responsive CIS output but does not establish direct STAT5 occupancy at the Cish promoter or an SCI receiver-cell endpoint; receptor stoichiometry and later disease contexts remain bounded

cell_type_context: microglia and relay neurons in the developing retinogeniculate circuit
context_scope: primary model context only; no SCI transfer inferred
assay_or_perturbation: microglial TWEAK loss-of-function; Fn14 conditional deletion; recombinant TWEAK and overexpression/rescue; spine and synapse readouts after visual experience
citation_note: Cheadle et al. 2020, Neuron; primary microglial TWEAK/neuronal Fn14 non-phagocytic spine-remodeling study
evidence_summary: The primary study supports a microglial TWEAK to neuronal Fn14 intercellular axis that changes bulbous-spine and retinogeniculate synapse abundance.
limitations: No intracellular cascade, TF, or direct target-gene expression was demonstrated; this is retained as an L-R-output route only and is not generalized to phagocytosis, traumatic SCI, or other receiver-cell contexts
